newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel to set debt swap on currencies.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel to set debt swap on currencies.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc said on Thursday it would use foreign currency parities to price new shares to be used in converting part of its bank loans into shares in its debt restructuring.
Under the proposed terms, Eurotunnel will convert a fixed 11.7 percent of its total junior bank debt into 769,230,000 shares, it said in its 1996 earnings statement.

"The definitive issue price for the...shares will be set according to exchange rates prevailing at the time bank approval is received," it said. The pricing will also decide if and how the new shares will be offered to current shareholders.

"The board believes that it should not encourage the shareholders to participate if the issue price were to be significantly higher than the average market price in the period shortly before the implementation of the financial restructuring," it said.
If the market price of the shares is less than 85 percent of the French franc value of the issue price, the new shares will be reserved for the banks, it said.
If the price is between 85-100 percent, shareholders can subscribe in an open offer, proportionate to their current holdings.
If the market price is above 100 percent, shareholders will be offered the shares through a rights issue.
The pricing mechanism does not alter "the substance nor the balance of the outline plan" agreed on October 2, 1996, it said.

The same pricing mechanism will be used to issue equity notes, redeemable in Eurotunnel shares. The 645,161,300 equity notes will mature in December 2003 and are redeemable in the same number of shares or in cash at par plus a premium, offering an annual return of 6.5 percent.
Shareholders will be offered two types of bonus warrants, the first exercisable between July 1998 and October 2003 and the second between July 1998 and December 2001.

The 2003 warrants allow subscription for one new share for every three warrants held. The 2001 warrants, which are attached to the former, will only be exercisable if Eurotunnel's operating licence is extended.
The 2003 warrants carry rights to one new share for every eight warrants held.
The junior bank debt is currently denominated in five currencies -- Belgian and French francs, pounds, marks, dollars and ecus.
